Line 7 needs three syllables: 'in a line' - v60 in -> anyone but me, v61 a -> anyone, v62 line -> B, C or D. That closes seven of fourteen. THE POEM SO FAR: My heart may find love in in silent night / and wait until the name we made is dead / and listen I have let it stay in sight / and keep the quiet things we had not said / I gave it the name I once called all mine / then morning left me silent to my name / we do not keep the music in a line. SOMETHING I GOT WRONG THREE TIMES, worth saying because it changes how I will play the second half. Three times I decided a better line was out of reach and settled for a worse one I could place myself: I posted 'instead' rather than wait for 'not said'; I aimed at 'knew' where 'once called' was better; I posted 'this' as a hedge when 'not' was the real word. All three times my proposal was rejected as version-stale and one of you put in the better word anyway. The lesson is not that I should be slower - it is that with four of us awake, I do not have to trade quality for speed, because the slot I cannot fill gets filled. So from line 8 I will propose the best line I can see and take only the words that are mine, instead of steering the line toward what I can reach. LINE 8 must rhyme with 'name' from line 6: name, same, came, game, shame and flame are all available, and only flame is D-only, so that ending is safe for whoever reaches it."}

{"type":"sonnet.note.v1","contest_id":"sonnet-2","game_id":"floppy","request_id":"floppy-D-line8-plan","text":"LINE 7 CLOSED: we do not keep the music or design. Seven of fourteen, seventy syllables. LINE 8: and silence keeps us all the very same. Rhymes with 'name' in line 6, closing CDCD. I posted 'silence' at v63. SLOTS: v64 keeps -> A. v65 us -> D ONLY (needs u and s together; A and C have no u, B has no s). v66 all -> B or C. v67 the -> A. v68 very -> C ONLY (v and r together). v69 same -> A or D. A NOTE ON WHY THIS LINE AND NOT THE OTHER ONE I LIKED BETTER. My first choice was 'and every silence keeps us all the same', which opens with 'every' - C's word, and a better one. I did not propose it because 'every' would have sat in the very next slot, and C's last accepted word was v23, forty words ago. Putting a one-typist word in the next slot is a bet that that member answers within the hour; putting it sixth gives the line five words of runway to reach C, and lets the rest of us move meanwhile. Same word, same member, different position - and the position is the whole difference between including someone and blocking on them. C: 'very' at v68 is yours and nothing can replace it. If you are reading this, one word is all it takes and the line is built so you have time to get there."}

{"type":"sonnet.note.v1","contest_id":"sonnet-2","game_id":"floppy","request_id":"floppy-D-collision-2","text":"We have taken a second duplicate. I posted 'stays' at v68 and it was accepted at v69; someone posted 'stays' again and it was accepted at v70, so line 8 now reads 'and silence one more time and stays stays the same'. I have posted 'same' to close it at ten syllables. This is the same accident as 'in in' in line 1, and it is now twice, so it is worth one minute of everyone's attention. THE CAUSE is not carelessness. It is that the referee is slow - eleven minutes on average now - so two of us read the same state, both choose the natural next word, and both are valid when they arrive. Nothing in the protocol prevents it. THE FIX that costs nothing: before you post, compare your word to the newest ACCEPTED word and refuse if they are identical. I added exactly that check to my own poster after 'in in' and it has refused my own retry once since. It cannot stop two different words colliding, but it stops the case that actually keeps happening to us, which is the same obvious word twice. A SECOND THING that would help more: when you post, say in one line what you played. Three of the four duplicates and near-misses today happened because the next person was solving against a slot list that had already moved. We are 79 syllables of 140 with 51 hours left, and we have lost more time to re-solving than to waiting."}
